title: Interview scrapbook - Nora Wei
content:
Candidate: Nora Wei (backend + inference infra)
Interviewers: Meera Iyer (owner), Samir Patel (SRE), Evelyn Torres (applied-ml)
Role: Senior Inference Engineer - serving runtime team
Stage: Onsite loop (system design + coding + culture)

Quick summary (top lines):
- Very strong systems instincts; thoughtful trade-offs on memory vs latency.
- Good on kernel-level awareness (CUDA/threading) but less confident about company-scale ops (SLOs, multi-tenant isolation policies).
- Coding was ok: solved core problem but missed a few micro-edge cases around concurrency.
- Communicates clearly, asks the right clarifying questions; pragmatic.

Detailed notes (raw):
- SD prompt: design a multi-tenant KV-cache layer for autoregressive models (supports TTL, hot-prefix caching, delta-eviction).
  - Nora sketched clear separation: in-process LRU + coordinated remote backing, consistent hashing for cross-GPU sharding.
  - Liked her idea of async refill with leaky-bucket rate limiter to avoid thundering herd. Good rationale for backpressure.
  - Brought up memory compaction and pointer-stability for KV tensors — nice low-level thinking.
  - Missed discussing warm-start for quantized model variants (we prob want explicit plan to populate w/ warm prefixes on deploy).

- Coding (30m): concurrency-safe bounded queue + token appender.
  - Implemented producer-consumer with locks; got deadlock scenario when consumer throws mid-batch.
  - When asked about lock-free alternatives, proposed SPSC ring buffer but couldn't fully flesh out ABA problem mitigation.
  - Timeboxed — overall passed but would need pairing to harden concurrency.

- Behavioral / culture fit:
  - Prefers small, focused teams; has shipped infra features end-to-end.
  - Shared examples of running rollback playbooks and paging incidents; comfortable with on-call.
  - Values shipping incremental improvements rather than big-bang rewrites — aligns with our runtime team.

Red flags / open concerns:
- Some gaps in production multi-tenant policy thinking (billing, soft isolation, noisy neighbor mitigation). Could be trained, but would require ramp.
- Not deep in our specific toolchain (e.g., our internal scheduler) — ok if we plan 1:1 onboarding.

Strengths:
- Systems-first engineer, low-level memory and performance intuition.
- Pragmatic tradeoff framing, communicates options well to PM/eng.
- Good debugging examples; solid incident postmortems cited.

Potential pairing areas / hiring level recommendation:
- Could fit Senior Engineer (IC3) with mentorship on product-side policy and high-scale ops. Strong candidate for IC3 -> IC4 within 6–12 months if paired with platform exposure.

Scorecard (quick, informal):
- System design: 4/5
- Coding: 3/5 (logic right, edge cases missed)
- Culture / ownership: 4/5
- Production ops: 3/5
- Communication: 5/5

Suggested next steps / notes for hiring committee:
- Recommend follow-up: small pairing session focused on concurrency hardening and a brief session with platform lead to gauge multi-tenant policy thinking.
- Ask for a short writeup (1 page) on how they'd approach prefix warming for quantized models in our infra — will show depth on domain-specific gaps.
- If we proceed to offer, target comp band: Senior (IC3) range; mention growth path to IC4 contingent on owning one large infra project.

Loose TODOs / action items (Meera):
- Ping platform lead (Aisha) to schedule 30m sync.
- Share loop notes + code snippet with interview panel for quick thumbs.
- Add Nora to candidate tracker (JIRA HIRE-482) and attach resume + GH link.

Misc scribbles / things I liked:
- Nora's async refill + leaky-bucket idea — could be prototyped as experiment on a single shard.
- Good mental model of KV pointer stability; could be useful for our cache compaction RFC.

Unanswered questions to surface to candidate if we move forward:
- Have you designed eviction policies that account for inference quality (not just recency/size)? Any off-the-shelf heuristics you used?
- How would you approach per-customer throttling to enforce quotas while staying fair across short vs long requests?

End of notes.

(Informal — meant for internal review only. Will tidy if we send to hiring committee.)
